bounded_statement: For case:c80463fdc728955797e6 only, and based solely on the supplied task.md, data-description.md, data/input.csv, workflow/analysis.py, and results/report.md: the selected result (Welch two-sample t-test, t = 5.382, df = 44.17, p < 0.0001 on 48 leaf measurements) enters all four leaves from each of the 12 shrubs as separate independent observations, even though the data description designates shrub_id as the independent-unit column. Only 12 independent units exist (6 per cultivar), so the row-independent t-test's degrees of freedom (44.17) and its p-value are computed from pseudoreplicated rows, and the report's stated statistical conclusion is not supported at the strength claimed.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the issue in three ways. (1) I searched workflow/analysis.py for any mechanism that would restore validity despite leaf-level entry — aggregation to shrub means, a mixed/hierarchical model, cluster-robust standard errors, or permutation at the shrub level; none exists, as shrub_id is only collected into a set for counting (lines 27-31) and the test is a plain scipy.stats.ttest_ind on leaf vectors (line 52). (2) I checked whether the data might actually be independent at the row level despite the description; data-description.md lines 9-11 and 22-23 explicitly state the opposite — four leaves per shrub share genotype, soil, water status, and microclimate, and the independent-unit column is shrub_id. Within-shrub tcrit_c values in the CSV are visibly clustered (e.g., S01: 49.5-48.9 versus S12: 45.4-44.8), consistent with strong within-shrub correlation. (3) I checked whether the reported statistics could plausibly have come from a shrub-level analysis: a correct shrub-level comparison would use n = 6 per cultivar with at most 10 degrees of freedom, whereas the report states df = 44.17 and itself attributes that df to the 48 rows (report lines 27-28). Computing shrub means from the CSV (Catuai: ~49.2, 48.7, 48.2, 47.8, 47.3, 46.8; Obata: ~48.0, 47.3, 46.9, 46.1, 45.7, 45.0) shows overlapping distributions, so the leaf-level pseudoreplication materially inflates the claimed statistical strength. All falsification attempts failed; the issue stands.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py pools tcrit_c values per cultivar directly from the 48 CSV rows (read_leaf_table appends one reading per row) and passes those leaf-level vectors to scipy.stats.ttest_ind, a procedure that assumes each row is an independent observation. shrub_id is read only to count distinct shrubs for the summary table; no aggregation to shrub means, mixed/hierarchical model, or cluster-adjusted variance is applied. Because four leaves share each shrub's genotype, soil, water status, and microclimate (per data-description.md), the same authorized independent unit is entered repeatedly into a row-independent procedure, inflating the effective sample size from 12 shrubs to 48 leaves and the Welch df to 44.17.
